turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Device Physics Analysis

**Key trends from the training data (300 configs, target range 0.03–20.85%):**

1. **ETL chemistry dominates the high-efficiency tail.** The single best training device (20.85%) uses **TiO2-c | SnO2-np** as the ETL. SnO2-based ETLs (SnO2-c, SnO2-np) repeatedly appear in the 13–20% band (e.g., 17.28, 17.47, 16.9, 14.72, 13.45), outperforming plain TiO2-c/TiO2-mp stacks on average. This fits the physics: SnO2's deeper conduction band edge and higher electron mobility give better band alignment and lower interfacial recombination with MAPbI3 than TiO2, and it avoids TiO2's UV-induced trap generation.

2. **Spiro-MeOTAD and PTAA are the only HTLs consistently found above 15%.** PTAA appears in some of the very highest points (18.9, 18.19, 15.9, 15.46), often paired with SnO2/oxide ETLs — PTAA's higher hole mobility and good HOMO match to MAPbI3 give efficient, low-recombination hole extraction.

3. **MoO3 interlayers before Au/Ag back contacts** show up repeatedly at the top (17.66, 17.5, 17.28, 18.965) — MoO3 improves hole selectivity/ohmic contact at the metal interface, suppressing back-contact recombination.

4. **Simple, well-controlled spin-coating (sometimes with a CBD rinse/post-treatment) correlates with the best results** — no exotic multistep depositions among the top values.

5. **Fullerene-based ETL/HTL combos (C60/PTAA/Ag or MoO3)** also cluster respectably (16.5, 17.9), showing selective-contact fullerene chemistry is a secondary viable route.

**Applying this to the candidate pool:**

- **c064** (TiO2-c | SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au) is almost a direct analog of the single best training recipe (TiO2-c | SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag/Dipp-coating, 20.85%) — excellent band alignment and low trap density expected.
- **c068** (SnO2-np | TiO2-np, PTAA, Au | MoO3) combines the two best-performing ingredients (SnO2 ETL + PTAA HTL) with a MoO3 buffer — matches the profile of the 18.9%/18.19% training entries.
- **c035** (SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3 | Ag | WO3) — SnO2 ETL + Spiro + MoO3 buffer, consistent with several 16–18% training devices.
- **c073** (TiO2-c | C60, PTAA, Ag) is essentially identical to a training recipe that gave 16.5% (TiO2-c | C60, PTAA, Au) — strong fullerene/PTAA selective-contact synergy.
- **c021** (SnO2-np | CPTA, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au) — SnO2-based ETL with an interfacial passivation additive (CPTA) plus Spiro/Au, matching the chemistry of the mid-to-high efficiency SnO2/Spiro cluster.

These five combine the two most reliable "efficiency-boosting" motifs seen in training (SnO2-type ETL, Spiro-MeOTAD/PTAA HTL, MoO3 buffer where present) more consistently than any other pool entries.

Final: c064, c068, c035, c073, c021
